O.outcome_detail: mQSAT assessment performance across primary assessment, diagnostic actions, therapeutic actions, communication, and global rating

cells.quote: For mQSAT scores (n=32), no statistically significant differences were observed between any of the study groups for any domain by ANCOVA analysis.
cells.note: The study was a randomized cluster-allocated pilot; it explicitly states that it was not powered to conclude noninferiority.

O.outcome_detail: recognition of septic shock in the assessment scenario

cells.quote: For the recognition of septic shock (n=32), no statistically significant differences were observed between groups by binomial test.
cells.note: Recognition was assessed after the assessment simulation; blinded reviewers agreed on the outcome.

O.outcome_detail: recognition of need for critical care

cells.quote: For recognition of need for critical care (n=32), a statistically significant difference was noted between the groups in participants who had received only 1 debrief (ie, 1 simulation session) prior to assessment. Participants who completed only 1 VR simulation and debrief prior to assessment were more likely to recognize need for critical care than those who completed only IP simulation and debrief (3/5 vs 1/7; P=.01).
cells.note: This significant result was limited to participants receiving one simulation session and debrief before assessment.

result.effect: No differences reported for any component

cells.quote: For the completion of the Sepsis 6 (n=32), no differences in performance were observed between any groups for any component by the Fisher exact test.
cells.note: The ancillary reviewer-agreement analysis reported slight-to-moderate Krippendorff α agreement (range −0.155 to 0.491), and sensitivity analyses using unblinded or all reviewers' scores did not change conclusions.
